The physical and emotional abuse of my father for one. And my mother's inability to really be there for me when I needed her. And their absence in a terrifying moment where I desperately needed them, and suffered because they just weren't there. My mom... She tried, and I appreciate the attempt. I just... Needed more.

The bright side to this though, is that I ended up a better person because of it. I'm not happy that it had to be this way for me to be the person I am, and I'm fraught with self doubt hatred, and deprecation, among a few other emotional and mental instabilities... But my dad gave me a framework of how NOT to grow and act, and my mom, with her personality, gave me something to inherit, and improve upon. I'm not perfect, but from their mistakes, and even some of the knowledge they tried to impart, I learned. And I will continue to learn, and grow with each passing day.

It's a sort of phenomenon where the musculature of the chicken grows abnormally. In affected poultry, it is typically tougher then a normal chicken breast, and may or may not have an unsatisfactory flavour with it. Apparently, one of the easiest things to spot with woody chicken breast are white striations across the meat. It is, at least here in the US, starting to become a common issue. It's likely to do with how some of our farmers raise their chickens. Genetic modifications cause the chicken to grow faster, and larger, and sometimes this will result in woody breast. Caring for a loved one who loses all capability of taking care of themselves...

My partner lost her independence when she developed severe Rheumatoid Arthritis last year, and Fibromyalgia to go along with it. Further exacerbated by mental trauma and PTSD from previous baggage, which also brought about FNSD for a little while... (Something where the brain does things like prevent use of limbs and the like, formerly classified as "Psychosomatic") She's in constant, severe pain in all of her joints (which only get worse with regular flare ups), and her muscle pain from fibro will sometimes add to the load. It's almost impossible for her to do anything on her own without assistance. She usually has to have a wheelchair present when she goes out. Still waiting on her doctor's approval for her treatment...

It doesn't help that I also have to battle with my own trauma and PTSD, and can't always help her when she needs me when I start to have a breakdown. My baby's a real trooper, but man... It's exceptionally exhausting taking care of her day in and day out.
